en: Paṭisambhidāmagga 3,
Paññāvagga 3.4.
Discourse on Seclusion (Vivekakathā)
At Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, just as whatever tasks requiring strength are performed, they are all done depending on the earth and established upon the earth;
even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, depending on virtue and established in virtue, develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.”
And how, monks, does a monk, relying on virtue and established in virtue, develop the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path?
Here, monks, a monk develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
He develops right intention... [and so forth].
right speech … right action … right livelihood …
He develops right effort … right mindfulness … right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
In this way, monks, a monk—relying on virtue and established in virtue—develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.

Just as, monks, whatever plants and seeds attain growth, increase, and abundance, they all do so by relying on the earth and being established upon the earth; even so these plants and seeds attain growth...
They reach growth, increase, and abundance.
In the same way, monks, a monk who— relying on virtue and established in virtue—
develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path reaches growth, increase, and abundance in wholesome qualities.

And how, monks, does a monk, relying on virtue and established in virtue, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path, attain growth, increase, and abundance in wholesome qualities?
Here, monks, a monk develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
He develops right intention... [and so forth].
He develops right speech… he develops right action… he develops right livelihood…
He develops right effort … he develops right mindfulness … he develops right concentration,
which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.

“It is in this way, monks, that a monk, relying on virtue and established in virtue, develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, thereby attaining growth, increase, and abundance in wholesome qualities.
3.4.1. Exposition of the Factors of the Path (Maggaṅganiddesa)
For right view there are five kinds of seclusion, five kinds of fading away, five kinds of cessation, five kinds of relinquishment, and twelve supports.
For right intention … [and] for right speech … [the same applies].
of one with right action … of one with right livelihood … of one with right effort …
For right mindfulness...
for right concentration, there are five kinds of seclusion, five kinds of fading away, five kinds of cessation, five kinds of relinquishment, and twelve supports.
What are the five kinds of seclusion for right view?
Seclusion by suppression, seclusion by substitution of opposites, seclusion by eradication, seclusion by tranquillization, and seclusion by escape.

Seclusion by suppression belongs to one developing the first jhāna as a means of suppressing the hindrances; seclusion by substitution of opposites belongs to one developing concentration partaking of penetration as a means of substituting the opposite to wrong views;
and seclusion by eradication belongs to one developing the supramundane path leading to the destruction [of the defilements].
For one who is developing [the path], there is the seclusion of subsiding at the moment of the fruit, and the seclusion of escape, which is cessation, Nibbāna.
These are the five kinds of seclusion for right view.
Toward these five kinds of seclusion, he becomes filled with desire, intent upon faith, and his mind is well-established.
In the case of right view, what are the five kinds of fading away?
Fading away by suppression, fading away by substitution of opposites, fading away by eradication, fading away by tranquillization, and fading away as escape.
Fading away by suppression is that of the hindrances for one developing the first jhāna; fading away by substitution of opposites is that of speculative views.
For one developing concentration partaking of penetration, there is fading away through cutting off;
for one developing the supramundane path leading to destruction, there is fading away through the fruit at the moment of fruition; and cessation, which is Nibbāna, is fading away through escape.
These are the five kinds of fading away associated with right view.
Regarding these five types of fading away, he has conceived a desire for them and is resolved through faith, and his mind is well-established therein.
What are the five cessations pertaining to right view?
Cessation by suppression, cessation by substitution of opposites, cessation by cutting off, cessation by tranquilization, and cessation by escape.
There is suppression-cessation of the hindrances for one developing the first jhāna; cessation by substitution of opposites of wrong views for one developing concentration partaking of penetration;
cessation by cutting off for one developing the supramundane path leading to the destruction [of defilements];
cessation by tranquilization at the moment of the fruit; and cessation as escape, which is the deathless element.
These are the five cessations for right view.
One becomes filled with desire for these five cessations, intent upon faith, and one’s mind is well-established.
What are the five relinquishments of right view?
Renunciation by suppression, renunciation by substitution of opposites, renunciation by cutting off, renunciation by tranquillization, and renunciation by escape.

Renunciation by suppression belongs to one developing the first jhāna as the suppression of the hindrances; renunciation by substitution of opposites belongs to one developing concentration partaking of penetration as the substitution of opposites for wrong views;
and renunciation by cutting off belongs to one developing the supramundane path leading to the destruction [of the defilements].
For one who is developing [the path], there is the relinquishment of tranquility at the moment of the fruit, and the relinquishment of escape, which is cessation, Nibbāna.
These are the five kinds of relinquishment associated with right view.
Regarding these five relinquishments, he becomes filled with desire and intent upon faith, and his mind is well-established.
For right view, there are these five seclusions, five dispassions, five cessations, five relinquishings, and twelve supports.
For right intention … [and] for right speech … [the same applies].
of one with right action … of one with right livelihood … of one with right effort …
Regarding right mindfulness… and right concentration, what are the five kinds of seclusion?
Seclusion by suppression, seclusion by substitution of opposites, seclusion by eradication, seclusion by tranquillization, and seclusion by escape.

Seclusion by suppression is for one developing the first jhāna as a means of suppressing the hindrances; seclusion by substitution of opposites is for one developing concentration partaking of penetration as a means of substituting the opposite to wrong views;
seclusion by eradication is for one developing the supramundane path leading to the destruction [of defilements];
seclusion by tranquillization is at the moment of the fruit; and seclusion by escape is cessation, Nibbāna.
These are the five kinds of seclusion for one of right concentration.
Toward these five kinds of seclusion, he has conceived desire, is resolved with faith, and his mind is well-established.
What are the five kinds of fading away for one of right concentration?
There is fading away by suppression, fading away by substitution of opposites, fading away by cutting off, fading away by tranquillization, and fading away as escape.

Fading away by suppression belongs to one developing the first jhāna in regard to the hindrances; fading away by substitution of opposites belongs to one developing concentration partaking of penetration in regard to views;
and fading away by cutting off belongs to one developing the supramundane path leading to the destruction [of the taints].
For one who is developing [right concentration], there is fading away through subsiding at the moment of the fruit, and fading away as escape, which is cessation, Nibbāna.
These are the five kinds of fading away for right concentration.
Toward these five kinds of fading away, he becomes filled with desire and intent upon faith, and his mind is well-established.
What are the five cessations of right concentration?
Cessation by suppression, cessation by substitution of opposites, cessation by cutting off, cessation by tranquilization, and cessation by escape.
Cessation by suppression is that of the hindrances for one developing the first jhāna; cessation by substitution of opposites is that of the various types of views.
For one developing concentration partaking of penetration, there is cessation by cutting off;

for one developing the supramundane path leading to the destruction [of defilements], there is cessation by tranquillization at the moment of the fruit; and the cessation by escape is the deathless element.
These are the five cessations of right concentration.
Regarding these five cessations, he becomes filled with desire and resolved through faith, and his mind is well-established.
What are the five relinquishments of right concentration?
They are: relinquishment by suppression, relinquishment by substitution of opposites, relinquishment by eradication, relinquishment by subsiding, and relinquishment by escape.
There is the abandonment by suppression for one developing the first jhāna [to suppress] the hindrances;

the abandonment by substitution of opposites for one developing concentration partaking of penetration [to abandon] views; the abandonment by cutting off for one developing the supramundane path leading to destruction;
the abandonment by tranquillization at the moment of fruition; and the abandonment by escape, which is cessation, Nibbāna.
These are the five relinquishments of right concentration.
Toward these five relinquishments, one becomes filled with zeal and intent upon faith, and one’s mind is well-established.
These are the five seclusions of right concentration, the five dispassions, the five cessations, the five relinquishments, and the twelve supports for right concentration.
“Just as, monks, whatever tasks requiring strength are performed, they are all done depending on the earth and established upon the earth;
even so, monks, a monk, depending on virtue and established in virtue, develops the seven factors of awakening and cultivates the seven factors of awakening...
developing the seven factors of awakening and cultivating the seven factors of awakening, he attains growth, increase, and abundance in wholesome qualities.”
He develops the five powers, he cultivates the five powers …pe… by developing the five powers and cultivating the five powers, he attains growth, increase,
and abundance in wholesome qualities …pe… he develops the five faculties, he cultivates the five faculties …pe….
Just as, monks, whatever plants and seeds attain growth, increase, and abundance,
they all do so by depending on the earth and being established upon the earth; it is thus that these plants and seeds attain growth,
increase, and abundance.

In the same way, monks, a monk who—relying on virtue, established in virtue—develops the five faculties and cultivates the five faculties extensively, attains growth, increase, and fulfillment in regard to the qualities.

And how, monks, does a monk—relying on virtue, established in virtue—develop the five faculties and cultivate the five faculties extensively so as to attain growth, increase, and fulfillment in regard to the qualities?
"Here, monks, a bhikkhu develops the faculty of faith, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
He develops the faculty of energy...
[as above] ...he develops the faculty of mindfulness... [as above]..."
He develops the faculty of concentration …pe… he develops the faculty of wisdom,
which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
It is in this way, monks, that a monk, relying on virtue …pe… [continues].
"...one attains [mastery] over phenomena.
3.4.2. Exposition of the Faculties (Indriyaniddesa):
For the faculty of faith, there are five kinds of seclusion, five kinds of fading away, five kinds of cessation, five kinds of relinquishment, and twelve supports.
Of the faculty of energy … [and so on] … of the faculty of mindfulness … [and so on] … of the faculty of concentration … [and so on] …

For the faculty of wisdom (paññindriya), there are five kinds of seclusion (viveka), five kinds of fading away (virāga), five kinds of cessation (nirodha), five kinds of relinquishment (vosagga), and twelve supports (nissaya).
What are the five kinds of seclusion for the faculty of faith (saddhindriya)?

They are: seclusion by suppression (vikkhambhanaviveka), seclusion by substitution of opposites (tadaṅgaviveka), seclusion by eradication (samucchedaviveka), seclusion by tranquilization (paṭippassaddhiviveka), and seclusion by escape (nissaraṇaviveka).
There is seclusion by suppression for one developing the first jhāna as the removal of the hindrances;

seclusion by substitution of opposites for one developing concentration partaking of penetration as the removal of views; seclusion by eradication for one developing the supramundane path leading to the destruction [of defilements];
seclusion by tranquillization at the moment of the fruit; and seclusion by escape is cessation, Nibbāna.
These are the five seclusions of the faculty of faith.
Toward these five seclusions, one becomes filled with desire and intent upon faith, and one’s mind is well-established.
… [as above] … These are the five seclusions of the faculty of faith; there are five dispassions, five cessations, five relinquishings, and twelve supports for the faculty of faith.
Of the faculty of energy …pe… of the faculty of mindfulness …pe… of the faculty of concentration …pe…
What are the five seclusions of the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*)?

The seclusion of suppression (*vikkhambhanaviveka*), the seclusion by substitution of opposites (*tadaṅgaviveka*), the seclusion by eradication (*samucchedaviveka*), the seclusion by subsiding (*paṭippassaddhiviveka*), and the seclusion of escape (*nissaraṇaviveka*). ... [as above] ...
These are the five seclusions, the five dispassions (*virāga*), the five cessations (*nirodha*), the five relinquishments (*vosagga*), and the twelve supports (*nissaya*) of the faculty of wisdom.
The Discourse on Discrimination is finished.
